subject: SOC 2 report and cloud provider scope alignment for Stratus Health
messages:
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@stratushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@stratushealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II + provider scope clarification

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor security review for Stratus Health, we need a copy of Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II report (covering the period Jan 1 2024 - Jun 30 2024) and clarification on how you’re handling cloud provider carve-outs. Our specific asks: 

- SOC 2 Type II PDF (signed) for the stated period.
- Bridge letter or confirmation if the SOC period doesn’t align with our audit window (we may require a statement covering up to Dec 31 2024).
- A mapping that shows which control areas are covered by your cloud provider reports (e.g., AWS/GCP SOC), and any areas that remain the responsibility of Redwood or your subprocessors (KMS, backups, customer key custody, etc.).
- Current list of subprocessors and whether any subcontracted services are within the scope of your SOC report.

Is it possible to provide these materials and a short note on the above by EOD Friday? If you prefer a quick call to walk through the mapping, we can do 30 minutes on Thursday afternoon.

Best,
Emily
Security Manager, Stratus Health
security@stratushealth.com

Attachments: none

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@stratushealth.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Aug 2024 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + provider scope clarification

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priya (CISO programs) and Karthik (infra/compliance mapping) to pull the artifacts and prepare a short mapping. Preliminary answers:

- We can provide our signed SOC 2 Type II report (we have a 2024 report covering Jan–Jun) and a bridge letter that can extend coverage language through Dec 31, 2024.
- We’ll supply a control mapping that shows which areas are covered by provider SOCs (AWS for compute/storage, GCP in specific regions) versus Redwood responsibilities (application-level access controls, customer data segregation, some KMS custody configurations).
- Subprocessor list is maintained in our vendor register; we’ll highlight which ones are in-scope for the SOC and which are outside.

Karthik — can you assemble an AWS/GCP coverage matrix and confirm whether our current KMS configuration is considered within provider scope or a Redwood-managed subprocess responsibility?

Emily — we plan to send the SOC PDF and a draft bridge letter tomorrow. If that meets your immediate needs, we can set a 30-minute call Thursday 2–2:30pm PT to walk the details.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2024 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC coverage notes + provider responsibilities matrix

Vanessa / Priya — FYI I've assembled the initial coverage matrix and notes below. Attaching a CSV with the itemized mapping. Key points: 

- AWS SOC 2 (latest) covers compute, EBS/S3 storage, network segmentation, and the managed RDS service we use. It does NOT cover managed KMS keys when customers bring their own key material or when we manage keys in a customer-dedicated HSM; in those cases Redwood is the subservice performing key custody operations.
- Backups stored in S3 are covered as storage by AWS SOC report; however, the backup encryption key custody and rotation is a Redwood operational process and not part of the provider SOC.
- Our IAM and application-level access controls are Redwood responsibilities; some provider controls (e.g., hypervisor isolation) are provider-covered.
- Current subprocessors in-scope for Redwood’s SOC: DataPipelineCo (ingestion), MetricsStream (telemetry processing). Those are included in our SOC scope. Third-party analytics/BI tools are not in scope.

Proposed customer-facing options: 
1) Provide SOC 2 Type II PDF + bridge letter that explicitly calls out the provider carve-outs and lists the subprocessors that are in-scope. This is the fastest route.
2) Provide SOC PDF + coverage matrix + offer an attestation call where we walk the sections and provide redlines to a bridge letter specific to your audit requirements.

I’ve attached "AWS_SOC2_coverage_matrix_2024.csv" for Stratus to review. If Priya confirms, we can produce the bridge letter draft and Redwood SOC PDF tomorrow afternoon.

Karthik
Sr. Manager, Cloud Reliability
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: AWS_SOC2_coverage_matrix_2024.csv

Hi Emily —

Thanks for your patience. Attached are the items we discussed: 

- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf (signed cover period Jan 1 2024–Jun 30 2024)
- Redwood_Bridge_Letter_Draft.docx (draft bridge letter that extends the statement through Dec 31 2024 and calls out provider carve-outs)
- AWS_SOC2_coverage_matrix_2024.csv (mapping of provider vs Redwood responsibilities, highlighted rows for KMS/backups/key custody)

Highlights & next steps: 
- The bridge letter explicitly notes that AWS SOC reports cover infrastructure and managed services (compute, storage, network) but not Redwood-managed key custody for customer-supplied keys or any manual key-handling procedures.
- Subprocessors included in Redwood's SOC: DataPipelineCo, MetricsStream. A full vendor register export can be provided if you need line-item dates or contracts.
- If you want to see a tailored bridge letter with your legal language, we’re happy to accept redlines. Otherwise, propose a 30-minute call to walk the mapping and answer any section-specific questions — available Mon 26 Aug 10–11am PT or Tue 27 Aug 2–3pm PT.
